title: Latency thermography weekly capture — 2026-10-06
content:
Meeting: Performance & Benchmarking Sync — Latency Thermography
Date: 2026-10-06
Facilitator: Aisha Patel
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Aisha, Miguel, Claire, Ravi, Elena, K. Osei (observability)

Purpose
- Capture weekly ‘latency thermography’ (mapping of latency behavior across sequence length, batch, kernel versions, and cache temperature).
- Triage recent tail regressions seen in production (P95/P99) and plan verification runs.

Agenda
1) Quick sync on today’s production signal (SLOs, recent alerts)
2) Recap of lab runs from 2026-10-05 (shadow and canary)
3) Hypotheses for tail regressions and design of narrow experiments
4) Action items and owners

Executive summary / TL;DR
- Production: small but consistent increase in P95/P99 for rw-instruct-13b workloads since 2026-10-02. Aggregate P50 unchanged.
- Lab reproduction: reproduced tail shifts in dedicated shadow cluster when kernel-compat package v2.3.1 was applied to nodepool-gpu-stable.
- Primary hypothesis: new GEMM kernel parameter defaults in v2.3.1 interact badly with mixed-seq long-token requests (>=512 tokens) causing microburst stalls at KV cache commits.
- Short-term mitigations: pin nodepool-stable to v2.3.0, increase KV flush backoff in canary (Ravi).
- Next runs: thermography sweep across sequence lengths [64,128,256,512,1024], batch sizes [1,2,4], and kernel versions [v2.2.9, v2.3.0, v2.3.1]. Shadow against production traffic window 09:00–12:00 PST on 2026-10-08 (Claire + Elena).

Production signal details
- Monitored route: /v1/generate (rw-instruct-13b pin)
- SLO: P95 <= 300ms, P99 <= 650ms for token generation step
- Observed (rolling 1h average, 2026-10-06 08:00–09:00 PST): P50 98ms (stable), P95 335ms (+18% vs baseline), P99 700ms (+15% vs baseline)
- Error rate: 0.04% timeouts (marginal increase)
- Related alerts: tail-latency-amber triggered 2026-10-04 03:14 UTC (investigation started)

Lab reproduction summary (2026-10-05 runs)
- Harness: benchharness v1.12.3, model artifact rw-instruct-13b:v2026-09-28, quant profile q8f-default
- Nodepools: nodepool-gpu-stable (kernel-compat v2.3.1), nodepool-gpu-canary (v2.3.0)
- Workload: mixed sequence distribution (30% short <=64, 50% mid 128–512, 20% long >=512), client qps ramp 0->600 requests/s, token-level measurement, open-loop generator to reproduce arrival patterns
- Key observations:
  - When v2.3.1 was applied, P95 increased ~20% for long sequence requests (>=512) at batch size 1. P50 unaffected.
  - Batch sizes 2 and 4 showed a different failure mode: throughput plateaued earlier and P99 spikes were correlated with periodic GC-like pauses on the host (not the python process).
  - KV cache hit-rate for long-chains dropped ~6% in v2.3.1 runs relative to v2.3.0 — attributable to timing windows where cache write/commit delayed the next request’s lookup by 1–2ms. That delay aggregates at scale causing tail amplification.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) GEMM kernel param change (v2.3.1) increases single-token matrix multiply latency for narrow-shaped mats at seq>=512 — cascading into KV commit backpressure. Evidence: microbench of GEMM shows 8–12% slower times for shapes matching 512-token attention heads. (Miguel lead)
2) Host kernel/userland scheduling interaction introduced by the driver update packaged in v2.3.1 — periodic spikes align with host cgroup reclaim windows on some instance types. Evidence: host-level iostat/cgroup traces show small correlate with pauses. (Claire lead)
3) Slight change in code path ordering in runtime v0.47 that together with v2.3.1 triggers earlier KV cache eviction/commit frequency. Evidence: instrumented traces show commit events shifted by ~1–2ms. (Ravi lead)

Narrow experiments to run (short, parallel)
- E1 (Miguel): Microbench GEMM shapes for 64/128/256/512 with both kernel versions. Collect 100k samples, compare latency distributions. Outcome: confirm or rule out kernel slowdowns. (ETA 2026-10-07 EOD)
- E2 (Claire): Run host-only stability test on affected instance types with kernel-compat v2.3.1 but without runtime changes — capture cgroup sched traces and CPU steal. (ETA 2026-10-07 midday)
- E3 (Ravi): Run benchharness with KV commit instrumentation toggled (disable speculative commit optimization) to see effect on tail. (ETA 2026-10-08 morning)
- E4 (Elena): Shadow run thermography sweep (all seq lengths and batch sizes) pinned to v2.3.0 and v2.3.1 back-to-back to capture end-to-end behavior under production-like arrival mix. (ETA 2026-10-08 09:00–12:00 PST)

Immediate mitigations (actions done or in progress)
- A1: Pin nodepool-gpu-stable to kernel-compat v2.3.0 (rolled 2026-10-06 10:40 PST). Status: rolled, monitoring. (Owner: SRE ops)
- A2: Increase KV commit backoff from 4ms -> 8ms on canary only to test smoothing effect. Status: applied to canary (Ravi).
- A3: Canary routing policy updated to avoid long-sequence heavy tenants for next 24h window. Status: applied (Product/Traffic team).

Open action items (owner, due)
- Miguel: Deliver GEMM microbench results and upload raw histograms. Due 2026-10-07 EOD.
- Claire: Host cgroup trace capture and quick analysis doc. Due 2026-10-07 15:00.
- Ravi: KV-commit-instrumented run and short writeup with traces. Due 2026-10-08 11:00.
- Elena: Orchestrate shadow thermography run and provide aggregated metrics dashboard (P50/P95/P99, KV-hit-rate, tail-sample traces). Due 2026-10-08 18:00.
- Aisha: Create EPIC ENGINF-3887 and link PR to potential rollback if v2.3.1 confirmed root cause. Due 2026-10-06 (done).

Notes from discussion
- We agreed that the short-term control is to pin the kernel and smooth KV commits; longer-term we should harden the runtime to be kernel-agnostic where possible (fallback vectorized GEMM, more conservative default params).
- Observability gaps: need better token-aligned KV cache timeline instrumentation (KVTimestamps) to see commit vs lookup delta per request. Action: Observability team to propose KVTimestamps schema (K. Osei).
- Consider adding a targeted canary traffic pattern that increases long-seq weight to detect regressions earlier in future rollouts. (Product/Traffic)

Follow-ups / next sync
- Quick check-in: 2026-10-07 10:00 (15m) to review Miguel & Claire early artifacts.
- Full thermography results review + decision on kernel rollback: 2026-10-08 16:00 (45m).

Appendix: quick metrics snapshot (aggregated from benchharness run 2026-10-05)
- v2.3.0 batch=1 seq=512: P50 96ms, P95 278ms, P99 590ms, KV-hit 92.1%
- v2.3.1 batch=1 seq=512: P50 100ms, P95 335ms, P99 710ms, KV-hit 86.0%
- v2.3.0 batch=2 seq=256: throughput 420 tok/s, P95 210ms
- v2.3.1 batch=2 seq=256: throughput 380 tok/s, P95 260ms
